title: Claims-port adapter, ACORD mapping profiles A/B, and fake core suite receiver
acceptance: adapters/index.mjs exports createAdapterService(ctx) returning { listAdapters, previewMapping, pushClaim, routes, init } as agreed with S1-INT-02
Claims-port interface { id, format, map(bundle, profile), send(payload, target) } with sample 'core-claims-suite' adapter registered

Two mapping profiles: A (Aurelia-style) and B (Kestrel-style), selected by tenant config integrations settings; each outputs ACORD-aligned JSON; unmapped[] and warnings[] reported; golden-file tests for both profiles
previewMapping(adapterId, claimId) returns { adapterId, format, payload, unmapped, warnings } without sending or writing core_sync
Built-in fake core receiver route POST /api/v1/integrations/fake-core/claims stores what it receives (tenant scoped) and returns a core claim number; GET to list received payloads for tests

pushClaim sends to the pluggable target (default: fake core, in-process or HTTP URL from config), records core_sync, and calls claims.setExternalRef; failure leaves core_sync status 'failed' and does not throw to the bus
claim.routed (or event named in claimsPort.pushOn) triggers pushClaim exactly once per event id; repeated with same payload hash is a no-op
brief: Build under src/modules/integrations/adapters/: index.mjs (createAdapterService), port.mjs (interface plus registry), core-claims-suite.mjs, profiles/{a,b}.mjs, acord-map.mjs (shared helpers), fake-core.mjs (receiver routes + tables fake_core_claims and core_sync). Interface contract with S1-INT-02: S1-INT-02 owns index.mjs/routes.mjs one level up and imports ./adapters/index.mjs; you return route definitions in the same shape the core runtime uses (see architecture/core-runtime-api.md) and register your bus handler in init(). Consume ctx.modules.claims.getClaimBundle, claims.setExternalRef, triage.getLatestTriage, coverage.getLatestVerification; in tests use small local fakes for these modules (no dependency on other teams' code). Read tenant config via ctx.tenants.get(...).integrations (claimsPort: { adapter, profile, target, pushOn }); default profile A, default pushOn claim.routed. ACORD alignment: use ACORD-style object names (ClaimsOccurrence, InsurancePolicy, Claimant, Loss, Vehicle/Property, AdjusterAssignment); profile A nests by ACORD aggregates with camelCase and ISO dates, profile B flattens with UPPER_SNAKE keys and YYYYMMDD dates and different coded loss-cause values - document both in a comment table. Payload must be deterministic (sorted keys) so the hash is stable. Pitfalls: PII appears in payload (intended, it goes to the carrier core) but never in logs or bus events; fake core must be tenant scoped; core claim numbers deterministic per tenant sequence, e.g. CC-<sequence>. Tests: tests/unit/adapters/{profile-a,profile-b,preview,push,fake-core}.test.mjs under tests/unit/integrations/adapters/, and tests/integration/integrations/adapters/core-push.test.mjs driving claim.routed through a real bus. Do not commit; write only your paths.
valueDrivers: Drop-in connection to carrier core claims system
Configurable mapping per tenant without code

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 33 unit+integration tests pass (golden A/B, preview, fake core, failure recording, once-per-event, tenant isolation)
